title: Meme Chaos Lab
premise: A neon meme-themed falling-particle sandbox where the player paints reactive materials into a digital lab chamber and watches them collide, flow, burn, and dissolve.
interaction_model: Direct pointer/touch sandbox painting with material selection, brush-size switching, pause/resume, and board reset.
objective: Create satisfying chaos by placing different matter types, experimenting with their interactions, and filling the chamber with emergent particle behavior.
progression: Open-ended free play with no formal levels; progression is self-directed experimentation, larger reactions, and remixing the board state through pause-and-purge cycles.
mood: Playful, flashy, reactive, and slightly chaotic
likely_audience: Players who enjoy casual sandbox toys, tactile simulation games, meme aesthetics, and touch-friendly pick-up-and-play experiences.
confidence_notes: High confidence on sandbox/cellular-automata mechanics because the code explicitly implements sand, liquid, fire, plant, stone, and acid behaviors on a grid.
High confidence on touch-first presentation because the UI emphasizes thumb-safe controls, pointer painting, and mobile-safe spacing.
Medium confidence on narrative framing because the meme-lab fantasy is primarily conveyed through naming, UI text, and audiovisual styling rather than explicit story systems.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a mobile-friendly browser game called 'Meme Chaos Lab' as a single-screen neon arcade sandbox where the player paints different materials into a full-screen pixel simulation chamber. Present a flashy sci-fi meme-lab aesthetic with a dark blue space-like background, glowing cyan/teal/violet UI, a large canvas, a start overlay, a pause overlay, a top HUD showing current chaos/particle count, and a bottom control area with three circular brush-size buttons plus a horizontally scrollable material palette. The core play loop should be freeform and tactile: the player taps or drags on the canvas to place the currently selected material, switches brush sizes for precision or spectacle, pauses at any time, and can purge the board to start fresh. Include seven tools/materials: erase/reset, falling sand-like grit, flowing water-like liquid, immovable stone blocks, static flammable plant matter, short-lived rising fire, and corrosive acid that can dissolve some neighboring matter. Simulate these on a low-resolution grid scaled up to the screen for chunky pixels, with sand falling and piling, liquids flowing sideways and downward, fire spreading to burnable cells and being extinguished by water, and acid occasionally corroding non-stone matter. Use ambient arcade background music and short responsive sound effects for start, selection, painting, blocked placement, pause, resume, combos, and clearing the board. Add celebratory reaction GIF popups or similar visual callouts when the player paints a dense combo or clears the chamber. Keep progression open-ended with no levels or victory state—the appeal should be experimentation, emergent reactions, rising chaos count, and satisfying audiovisual feedback in a polished touch-first presentation.
